sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: Appointed following the devastating Great Famine of 1876-78, which exposed the inadequacy of existing relief mechanisms.
• **Core Philosophy**: Shifted focus from 'charity' to 'state obligation' while maintaining the **Laissez-faire** economic stance.
• **Institutionalization**: Recommended the creation of a **Famine Code** to standardize relief operations across provinces.
• **Key Metric**: Emphasized the development of **Irrigation Infrastructure** and **Railway connectivity** as the primary long-term famine mitigation strategies.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Introduction of Famine Codes in every province
Standardized wage rates and work-for-food programs
Expansion of Railways and Irrigation canals
Market integration to move food from surplus to deficit areas

items.definition: A comprehensive manual detailing the duties of officials, criteria for declaring famine, and the scale of relief to be provided.
A financial mechanism created to set aside revenue specifically for famine relief, though often diverted for other colonial administrative expenses.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Administrative Standardization**: Uniformity in relief across British India.
• **Data Collection**: Systematic collection of agricultural statistics to predict crop failure.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Neglect of the 'purchasing power' of the peasantry; focus remained on market supply rather than affordability.
• **Solutions**: Later commissions (Lyall, MacDonnell) had to address the failure of the Strachey Commission to prevent mass mortality.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-I-R' (Strachey, Irrigation, Relief).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Strachey Commission (1880) prioritized Irrigation and established the first Relief Code.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Strachey Commission (1880) with the MacDonnell Commission (1900). Remember: Strachey was the FIRST, MacDonnell was the one that emphasized 'Village-level' relief.

Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Colonial Famine Policy' to describe the shift from reactive relief to bureaucratic management, noting that it failed to address the structural causes like high taxation and commercialization.

keyTakeaways: The Strachey Commission was the first systematic attempt to codify famine relief in India.
It emphasized infrastructure (Railways/Irrigation) over direct food distribution.
It established the 'Famine Code' which became the blueprint for subsequent colonial famine management.
